title: Two requests in flight on the RTX 5090: eight-token verify rounds left the Q5 tensor-core route, and running them on it takes two decoding requests from 1.14x to 1.69x of one at a time with byte-identical outputs
question: Can the RTX 5090 lane serve two requests at once (--max-concurrency 2, OMP maxInFlightRequests 2 for its providers) with more aggregate decode, the same outputs, and no loss of prefix reuse, durable sessions, 130,048-token retrieval or stock OMP's subagents and compaction? What limits it, and what does a second request cost the one already running?
answer: Yes for decode throughput, outputs, reuse and the durability paths measured so far; the v0.8.7 lane set on the final profile is incomplete. The published v0.6.13 image fits two requests (KV 160,256 tokens, 30,244 MiB of 32,607) but two decoding requests reached only 190.0-191.1 tok/s together against 166.7-167.1 one at a time: with two requests the MTP3 verify round carries eight tokens, and the Q5 projections left the four-token tensor-core route for SIMT kernels (12.8 ms of a 23.9 ms round, against 5.2 ms). Runtime e20060b6 runs them on that route at eight tokens: two decoding requests reach 282.0-282.8 tok/s together (146.0-151.3 each), one request alone is unchanged, and all 89 role-corpus cases run two at a time, like every probe request whose prompt and reuse path matched its one-at-a-time counterpart, are byte-identical to one request at a time. A request that does not fit beside the running one waits at the server, and at the default 30 s it expired; --pending-timeout-ms 180000 lets it wait while the wait plus the longest root prefill (130,048 tokens in 58.6 s) stays inside OMP 18.4.0's 300 s stream watchdog. On that profile the role corpus, profile gates, stock OMP durable sessions, EXP-072's long sessions, checkpoint reclamation and the EXP-050 workload passed. Stock OMP at limit 2 finished a parent's two scout subagents 22.8% sooner, and two short sessions started together 12.9% later: their simultaneous first turns each took about 3.4 s against 0.9 and 1.8 s one at a time. A decode beside another request's long prefill still slows to about 30 tok/s, and a request arriving while a prefill is staged waits for it. The third window ended when the appliance's C: drive filled and the WSL distro went read-only; the workload resume, barrier, fanout/restore probes and agent mix did not run on the final profile.

method.lane: RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB) on the production appliance, one engine-window arm at a time on port 18099 with a scratch checkpoint root. Each window took the supervisor hold, stopped production (ninfer-5090-v070p), armed an appliance-side dead-man restore, ran its arms, restored production and released the hold.

candidate_window.outputs: 31 of the 35 probe requests that completed in both c1pkg and c2pkg produced byte-identical outputs, including both requests of each decode pair, the decode beside a prefill and every fanout branch; the shipped image's C2 pair outputs differed. The 4 that differed are two-session continuations that took a different reuse path (a root re-prefill in one arm, the replayed continuation in the other) or carried a different previous turn; the same prompt on the same path gave the same output in both arms. The 89-case role corpus run two cases at a time answered all 89 byte-identically to the published v0.6.13 image one at a time

host_incident.what: At 17:17:53Z, during the final-profile window's workload resume, the appliance's Windows C: drive filled (NTFS event 141: 3.45 GB free, all of it reserve). The Ubuntu WSL distro's dynamically expanding ext4.vhdx (932 GiB) lives on C:, so VHDMP failed a write with 0xC000007F and unsurfaced the disk; ext4 went emergency read-only and the distro's binaries returned I/O errors.
host_incident.cause: Inside the distro ext4 reported 122 GB free, but C: backed only a few tens of GB of growth. This campaign's window arms left about 88 GB of checkpoint roots in the distro, and the reclamation step alone writes about 40 GB of checkpoints.
host_incident.effect: SSH to the distro, the window's own restore and its dead-man (which runs in the same distro) all failed; production stayed down.
host_incident.recovery: wsl --terminate left the distro unstartable (Wsl/Service/CreateInstance/E_UNEXPECTED); wsl --shutdown restarted the VM, ext4 recovered its journal (13 orphan inodes), Docker Desktop recovered by itself, the campaign's arm checkpoint roots were deleted (ext4 free 33 to 120 GB; C: free 29 GiB, since the vhdx does not shrink), and window.sh restore recreated production, healthy at 17:32:00Z.
host_incident.closure: window.sh start now refuses an arm unless C: has 64 GiB free, the window scripts check the same before stopping production, and each window deletes its arms' checkpoint roots on exit

restoration.window_3: 16:43:38-17:32:00Z (48.4 min), of which 14.1 min after the host failure at 17:17:53Z

decisions.runtime: RTX 5090 runtime candidate v0.6.14 from e20060b6 (alphastorm/ninfer perf/c2-q5-t8-mma): the Q5 small-T tensor-core route at eight tokens
decisions.profile: the v0.9.0 RTX 5090 profile adds --max-concurrency 2 --pending-timeout-ms 180000 (configuration cf1de114, deployment qwen38-5090-v0.9.0); the route config sets ninfer-beta and ninfer-main to 2 and keeps the RTX 4090 providers at 1
decisions.pending_timeout: 180 s, not 240 s: a waiting request emits nothing after response.created, and 240 s plus a 58.6 s root prefill would reach OMP's 300 s stream watchdog
decisions.invariants: tests/test_manual_tunnel_scripts.py binds each provider's limit to its lane's --max-concurrency and bounds a two-request lane's pending timeout inside OMP's watchdog
decisions.gate: publication waits for the remaining lane steps on the final profile, which need at least 64 GiB free on the appliance's C: drive

limits: One run per configuration and two repetitions per probe scenario, on synthetic prompts at thinking low.

Two requests share the KV pool only while both prompts plus their output reservations fit in 160,256 tokens (the reservation is prompt plus max_output_tokens minus one, request_plan_impl.h). OMP sends max_output_tokens 32768, so by that rule two OMP sessions above about 47K tokens each take turns [inference from the admission code; not measured with OMP].
Two alternating 62.4K-token sessions re-prefilled 2 of their 4 continuations from root at C2, as at C1; C2 does not raise how many long sessions keep their cache.
A decode beside another request's 71,641-token prefill ran at 30.4-30.5 tok/s with 479-481 ms output gaps, and a request arriving while a prefill is staged waits for it (26.7 s).

The concurrency probe, restart-with-two-in-flight and stock OMP parallel proofs ran with a 240 s pending timeout, not the final 180 s; the final profile's lane set is incomplete (see final_profile_window.not_run).
Stock OMP's compaction on the RTX 5090 fragment is snapcompact, with no model request, so these runs do not exercise a background summary overlapping a turn on this lane.
